text:
incident-bot: ALERT: SLO burn-rate alert firing for svc-inference-proxy (inference-proxy). Multi-window summary: 5m burn=210%, 1h burn=85%, 15m burn=160%. Pager criteria evaluated -> paging on. Incident ID: INC-2026-391. Dashboard: https://redwood.monitoring/d/infra/slo-burn?orgId=1&panelId=23

mira: ack — I'm taking primary. pinging @devin for model routing look. I'll gather customer impact now. :eyes:

devin: on it. quick scan of routing logs shows spike in 503s around 11:02-11:06 UTC, seems correlated with the new routing rule we pushed at 10:58. logs: ```ERROR 503 route_selector failed: KV cache miss overflow```

sasha: customer-impact note: hosted-api customers hitting elevated p95 latency (from 450ms -> 1.8s) and some requests returned 503. Support tickets rolling in (5 high-priority). marking as "customer-visible" in incident tracker.

mira: mitigation idea: temporarily disable routing change and enable fallback model variant for prod traffic. throttling non-prod traffic to reduce pressure. commands I'll run: ```
# disable new routing and rollback
redwoodctl routes update svc-inference-proxy --disable-rule=canary-route-2026-03-14
redwoodctl rollout rollback svc-inference-proxy --revision=2026-03-14-11
# throttle non-prod to 70%
redwoodctl traffic adjust --env=nonprod --ratio=0.7
```

incident-bot: ACTION: Manual suppression of pager for svc-inference-proxy for 10m while mitigation in progress (suppressed by mira). Note: automated alerts still logged.

tim: quick thought — we keep getting noisy pages from short, sharp 5m spikes. proposal: change paging logic to multi-window rule. Page only when either: (A) 5m burn > 200% AND 1h burn > 120%, OR (B) sustained 15m rolling burn > 150%. That should reduce pages on transient blips but still catch sustained regressions.

ana: +1 to multi-window. also propose adding an "impact" dimension to the paging decision: only page if (error rate OR latency) AND tagged customer-impact=true OR if support-ticket-count>3. Otherwise send a non-paging channel update.

sasha: I'll spin up a dashboard and create the follow-up ticket. INF-345 created: "Alert tuning: SLO burn multi-window + paging policy". Will include graphs for 5m/15m/1h burns, p95 latency, and support-ticket correlation.

mira: rollback completed at 11:07 UTC, fallback route enabled. early metrics look better. p95 trending down. I'll continue watching for 20m.

tim: leaving a runbook note for the handoff — @mira, if burn drops below 120% over 1h keep monitoring and file RCA. If burn persists > 150% 15m then escalate to platform oncall and page. I'm next shift in 30m, I'll take post-incident follow-up.

devin: post-incident action items (to be added to INF-345):
- [ ] update alert rule to multi-window paging logic described above
- [ ] add dimension filter: require customer-impact OR support-ticket-count>threshold for paging
- [ ] build synthetic test to catch routing rule regressions (nightly)
- [ ] add dashboard panel showing side-by-side 5m/15m/1h burn comparisons and annotation of deploys
- [ ] add note to oncall playbook about temporary suppression and allowed manual suppression durations

incident-bot: UPDATE: mitigation successful. p95 latency back to baseline (~480ms) and 1h burn now 30%. Paging suppressed ended. Closing incident INC-2026-391 and linking follow-up INF-345: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-345.

sasha: I'll own the alert rule PR. expect a draft tomorrow morning. tagging @tim and @ana for review. :thumbsup:

mira: thanks team. handing off to @tim for follow-up. I'll capture a short note in the post-incident channel in 30m.

tim: got it. will pick this up and drive the tuning PR. thanks everyone. :pray:
